summary.text: 妹 combines 女, which marks a female-person category, with 未 as a sound element. Its common meaning is “younger sister.” Some early uses have been read as 昧, “before daybreak”; if so, the graph may have been reused for a different word with a similar sound, though that reading is disputed.

formation.text: 妹 is a phonosemantic compound: 女 contributes the female-person category, while 未 supplies a sound cue. This analysis is also applied to early forms, though some inscription readings are disputed.

components.text: 女 marks the female-person category in 妹. No distinct earlier form or graphic change for this component is specified.
未 is identified as the phonetic component. Two reconstruction systems show a historical sound comparison with 妹; these are reconstructions, not direct recordings of ancient speech.

sound.text: In the Zhengzhang Old Chinese system, 未 *mɯds and 妹 *mɯːds are similar reconstructed forms.
In the separate Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese system, 未 *m[ə]t-s and 妹 *C.mˤə[t]-s provide another comparison.

history.text: Forms are documented in oracle-bone, bronze, seal, and clerical scripts. These labels show forms from different periods but do not by themselves establish a continuous sequence of graphic changes.
The traditional analysis treats 未 as the sound element. An older explanation associated 妹 with 末, but the evidence does not show that 未 arose through graphic corruption of 末.

uncertainties.text: Some oracle-bone uses and the bronze phrase 女妹辰 have been read as referring to 昧, “before daybreak.” Other readings include a place name, and the bronze phrase has also been interpreted as referring to childhood. These readings do not establish a semantic path to “younger sister.”

Reconstructions support a historical sound comparison between 未 and 妹, but ancient pronunciation was reconstructed rather than directly recorded; modern Mandarin readings alone do not prove the ancient relationship.
Comparative proposals linking 妹 to other language families are listed, but their evidence is not assessed here.

senses.period: attested in bronze inscriptions; exact date of the cited example unresolved
senses.text: A bronze inscription is read with the kinship sense “younger sister,” also given in the historical gloss 女弟. This does not establish the spoken word’s earliest meaning.

senses.period: oracle-bone and bronze inscription readings; phrase interpretation disputed
senses.text: Some early forms and a bronze phrase are interpreted as 妹 used for 昧, “before daybreak” or “dawn twilight.” If this is a borrowing, the graph was reused for a different word because the words sounded alike or similar; the old word’s pronunciation and its relation to the kinship word are not established.

senses.gloss: younger female relative of the same generation
senses.text: Historical dictionary examples attest 妹 for a younger female relative of the same generation. The evidence does not date this sense or derive it from “younger sister.”
A broader use meaning “young woman” is attested, but its chronology and relation to the kinship sense are not established.

senses.gloss: modest first-person reference by a woman
senses.period: later literary use; exact dating unresolved
senses.text: Historical examples attest 妹 as a woman’s modest first-person reference. The evidence does not establish when or how this usage developed.

limitations.text: The early readings do not establish whether the dawn-related use belonged to the same spoken word as the kinship sense or whether the graph was reused for a different word. If it was reused, the proposed mechanism is that the words sounded alike or similar; the old word’s pronunciation is not established here.
The broader and literary senses are attested, but the available examples do not establish their chronology or paths of development.

Early oracle-bone forms of 妹 have been interpreted as referring to dawn, but some readings identify a place name instead. The bronze phrase 女妹辰 also has competing interpretations, and the available evidence does not establish a chronological path between the disputed dawn reading and the kinship sense “younger sister.”
